Currently I have C:2, B:0, A:1. Trading away my only A (dropping to 0) for a B (going from 0 to 1) keeps variety balanced - I'd have C:2, B:1, A:0, same total imbalance as before but diversifies from having zero B to having some. Since I value variety and currently have zero B while having 1 A, gaining B while losing A moves me from (2,0,1) to (2,1,0), which is symmetric in imbalance. However since B is scarcer for me now (0) than A (1), acquiring B raises marginal utility more than losing A costs, making this a net positive trade under diminishing marginal value per good type."
